claim: On 16 May 2024 the Swedish government assigned the Swedish Food Agency (Livsmedelsverket) to compile and spread knowledge about the role of food and meals in preventing ill health among older people, including guidance material for elderly care staff and decision makers. The assignment reports by 15 June 2026.
source_note: Found via regeringen.se search for 'halsosamt aldrande'. Press release from Socialdepartementet, minister Anna Tenje quoted on meals strengthening health and preventing illness.

claim: Forte, the Swedish government research council for health, working life and welfare, awarded about SEK 160 million to research on older people's health and wellbeing: three six-year programme grants and 19 project grants running 2023-2029, decided under the call 'Kunskap och arbetssatt for ett mer jamlikt, delaktigt och vardigt aldrande'.
source_note: Forte's own announcement (forte.se/nyhet/161-miljoner-till-forskning-om-aldres-halsa-och-valbefinnande/) currently returns 404, so the Karolinska Institutet news item is used as the working source; it names the REALM programme grant (SEK 23,819,000, Lena Dahlberg) and totals.

claim: Forte, commissioned by the Swedish government to coordinate national research on ageing, co-funds a NordForsk call on sustainable health and care systems for the elderly. Five Nordic-Baltic research projects were selected for funding out of 74 applications, announced 5 June 2025.
source_note: Found via search for Forte national research programme on ageing. Forte English news item; page states Forte's government commission to coordinate ageing research.

claim: The Swedish National study on Aging and Care (SNAC), launched in 2001 on the initiative of the Swedish government, is a still-running national longitudinal study following over 8,000 older adults in four areas (Blekinge, Kungsholmen, Nordanstig, Skane) to answer questions about future care needs.
source_note: Swedish national data catalogue (researchdata.se, formerly SND) record; published 2015-10-21, last updated 2026-04-15. The record states the 2001 launch by government initiative. Older URLs snd.gu.se/en/catalogue/study/ext0124 and snd.se redirect here.

claim: Karolinska Institutet participates in UNION, an EU Horizon Europe MSCA doctoral network on understanding frailty towards healthy ageing (grant 101167421), running 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2028, with an EU contribution of EUR 587,419 to KI out of EUR 3,423,240 total.
source_note: CORDIS project fact sheet, found via CORDIS search for Horizon Europe healthy ageing projects with Swedish participants. Source date is the project start date shown on the fact sheet.

claim: Sweden's Minister for Older People and Social Insurance, Anna Tenje, visited South Korea and Japan from 30 September 2024 to discuss demographic change, healthy ageing, elderly care, pensions and dementia, saying she looked forward to discussing what the countries can learn from each other on ageing populations.
source_note: Regeringen.se press release; programme included the Korea-Sweden Age Well Forum and an international dementia seminar in Japan.

claim: The Swedish government's research and innovation bill for 2025-2028 (Prop. 2024/25:60, published 12 December 2024) raises state research funding by a cumulative SEK 6.5 billion to 2028 and names health as one of the societal challenges requiring research investment.
source_note: Government proposition page on regeringen.se. Health is a named priority; ageing and longevity are not called out explicitly in the bill's summary, hence medium confidence on relevance. See se-008 for the ageing-relevant funding detail.

claim: Within the 2024 research and innovation bill, the Swedish government directs about SEK 600 million through 2028 to life science and health research, including dementia research, precision medicine, mental health and women's health, announced 18 December 2024.
source_note: Regeringen.se press release by the ministries of climate/enterprise, health and education. Dementia research funding is explicitly listed.

claim: Government bill Prop. 2025/26:60 'Starkta insatser for aldre och for de som vardar eller stoder narstaende' (20 November 2025) proposes Social Services Act amendments including a fixed care contact for older people in special housing and strengthened municipal support for family carers, entering into force 1 July 2026.
source_note: Riksdagen document page for the proposition; found via riksdagen.se search on elderly care legislation.

claim: The Riksdag Committee on Health and Welfare's report 2024/25:SoU21 on elderly care, decided 19 March 2025, handled about 60 motions covering elderly care organisation, healthcare in elderly care and dementia strategy, and notes that interventions should be coordinated to promote health and prevent ill health.
source_note: Parliamentary committee report (betankande), part of the legislative process though most motions were rejected citing ongoing work. Medium confidence on classification: it is a chamber decision on motions, not a new statute.

claim: In Riksdag motion 2021/22:4170 (5 October 2021), Christian Democrat leader Ebba Busch and colleagues argued that health-promoting strategies for older people are crucial for maintaining functional capacity, proposing 'senior health' physical activity programmes, preventive conversations for people over 80, and osteoporosis prevention.
source_note: Riksdagen motion page; submission date shown as 'Inlamnad: 2021-10-05'. An opposition party position paper, hence classified as political statement rather than policy.

claim: On 21 January 2025 the Swedish government presented the developed national dementia strategy 'Varje dag raknas' for 2025-2028, covering prevention, diagnostics, healthcare, dental care and social services, backed by SEK 100 million for 2025-2027 for regional collaboration structures.
source_note: Regeringen.se press release; ministers Anna Tenje and Jakob Forssmed. Strategy document itself: regeringen.se/informationsmaterial/2025/01/varje-dag-raknas-nationell-demensstrategi-20252028/.

claim: On 27 March 2024 the Swedish government assigned the Public Health Agency (Folkhalsomyndigheten) to map older people's mental health and wellbeing with a focus on their life situation, so that more targeted preventive measures can be put in place; the final report was due 1 September 2025.
source_note: Regeringen.se press release with social minister Jakob Forssmed quoted on listening to older people's own experiences.

claim: On 1 September 2026 the Public Health Agency of Sweden published government-commissioned recommendations for organisations working with people 65 and older, aimed at promoting mental health, preventing mental ill health and strengthening older people's resilience, including countering ageism and enabling active, meaningful daily lives.
source_note: Public Health Agency news item stating the recommendations were developed on the government's assignment; found via search on Folkhalsomyndigheten healthy ageing work.
